evidence: M-O s.v. edit (prepare a text for publication)
terms.comment: To free a text of faults (mendum, a slip of the pen): the word for correcting and revising writing and speech, and for editing a text in the scholar’s sense. Also, generally, to put right, reform (a habit, a city).
To straighten, put right a mistake (mendam corrigere, Comen. OP 97, the master at school); of a draft, as the critic in Horace marks line after line.

evidence: Cic. Ac. 1.2: quae līmantur ā mē polītius (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally to file (līma, a file); of writing, to polish it.

evidence: Suet. Aug. 34: lēgēs retractāvit; Plin. Ep. 8.21.6 (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To handle again, rework: a passage of a speech, a book before it goes out.
Traupman gives it for “edit”, but classically it is to publish, to give a book out to the world; an edition is ēditiō (see version), an editor redāctor (see editor).

phrases.latin: quaedam īnstituī, quae līmantur ā mē polītius
phrases.english: I have begun some things, which I am polishing with more care

phrases.latin: Quīdam sedent ad mēnsam, et scrībunt; ipse corrigit mendās.
phrases.english: Some sit at the table and write; the master himself corrects the mistakes.
